answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases hence burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the echo deposit is held in the reef escrow, the wharf audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 39 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. The deposit is 30 dollars a seat. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
